quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What color are the road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate lanes where traffic moves in opposite directions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells you a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are traveling at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the most effective way to protect yourself from death or injury while driving.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have and show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when stopped. These three documents are required in your vehicle when driving.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention from driving, removes your eyes from the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A community service group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or very close to the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are usually diamond-shaped, orange with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: May pass a slow-moving vehicle if you can do so quickly.
May pass if you know the road ahead.
May pass, but only at night.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white, rectangular signs with black markings. You must obey them. Where this sign is posted, passing other vehicles is not allowed.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. If you don't follow them, you can be fined.

questions.question: Night driving requires more caution because:

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
You cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so you cannot see as far ahead as during the day. From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, you must use your headlights. You must also use them whenever you cannot see people or vehicles 500 feet away.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop and wait for all vehicles and pedestrians to move before you go.

questions.question: An eight-sided sign is always a:
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs are always stop signs. Stop completely when you see a red eight-sided sign.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of wrecked vehicles.

questions.explanation: You must stop at or near the accident. Move your vehicle away from traffic if you can. Don't stand in traffic lanes because another car could hit you. Turn off engines in damaged vehicles.

questions.question: When can you pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk?

options.text: When the vehicle doesn't speed up quickly after the pedestrian leaves.
When the pedestrian is directly in front of the vehicle.
When you don't see a pedestrian.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Always assume the vehicle is waiting for a pedestrian, even if you don't see one.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection and be ready to stop. Let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: You should watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller than cars, so drivers often miss them even when looking. They may move faster and have less visible lights. Always stay alert for these road users to avoid collisions.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, not what the flagger says.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow the normal traffic rules as if construction is not happening.

questions.explanation: When a flagger directs you in a construction zone, you must obey. Slow down and follow their instructions. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: Your crash risk increases after you drink:
questions.explanation: Even one drink makes you more likely to crash. You cannot drink any alcohol and drive safely, no matter how much experience you have.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your car starts to skid, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. When the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. But you must let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection cross first.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means the same thing as:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Let all other traffic go before you move.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Stay at your normal freeway speed until you move onto the exit ramp. Then slow down.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly. Even with one track, check again for another train before crossing.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Do not move your vehicle at all.
Wait for police before moving your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: Move your vehicle off the road after a minor accident if possible. Do not leave the scene without giving your name and helping if needed.

questions.question: At an intersection with a stop sign but no markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet on both sides, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can see traffic coming before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see traffic coming before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting road where you can see traffic coming. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: You see flashing lights at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop your vehicle at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for a train, a lowered gate, or listen for a horn.

questions.question: When can you drive in a lane with a red X signal above it?

options.text: If there is no oncoming traffic.
If you are passing a car.

questions.explanation: A red X above a lane means that lane is closed. Never drive in a lane with a red X. These signals show which lanes are open or closed throughout the day.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that traffic on this street moves in only one direction. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.
Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.
Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
questions.explanation: If another car is following you too closely, slow down gradually and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely. Check your mirrors often to see what is behind you.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, a driver should:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the highway.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When you enter a highway from a ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when there is an open space in traffic.

questions.question: When a traffic light is broken, drivers should:

options.text: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
Treat the intersection as a roundabout.
Drive without stopping but proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop. The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.

questions.question: After a school bus stops and lets children off, you should:

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After a school bus stops and children get off, watch for them walking on the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows rules you must follow. You cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show direction and distance to destinations.
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show direction and distance to specific places. They help you when you are driving in an unfamiliar area.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of these except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Your level of physical fitness does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: You should drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
Entering a highway where there are other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: When the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions difficult, drive below the posted speed limit. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign with a yellow background. It warns you that a T intersection is ahead. Be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?
questions.explanation: When turning left from a multilane street or highway, always start from the left lane.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They can stop faster than cars.
They need the same space to turn as cars.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Avoid these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars because they are larger and heavier.

questions.question: When exiting the highway, when should you start to slow down?

options.text: When you turn on your blinker to enter the deceleration lane.
When you see your exit coming.
After you turn into the deceleration lane.
When you reach the end of the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you turn into the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Use the deceleration lane to slow down before your exit. This lane is made for you to reduce speed safely without putting other drivers at risk.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: Held safely by a strong adult.
Standing on the floor in the back.
They will be fine because they are small.
They must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats designed for their size. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always use a proper seat for children.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs show?
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you about railroad crossings. Let trains cross first—never try to beat a train.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign means pedestrians may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards on the road ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and sides constantly.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and sides constantly.
questions.explanation: Spot problems early so you can handle them safely. Scan ahead and to the sides, not just the center. This helps you see hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces this risk.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than day driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do after setting the parking brake?

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Turn the steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn the steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, set the parking brake and turn the steering wheel away from the curb. If the car rolls, it will roll toward the curb and stop.
